Trace and norm of an element of a finite field extension are respectively trace and determinant of the SAME K-linear multiplication endomorphism m_α:L→L, x↦αx. Trace versus determinant is a property applied afterward, not a different multiplication map.

Open and closed norm-ball source statements use the exact same displacement norm ∥v−a∥ in a normed vector space. Strict versus weak inequality belongs to the ball definition, not to the norm expression.

The geometrically-integral source uses K equal to an algebraic closure of k, a special field extension; the geometrically-regular source describes the general extension-of-scalars K-algebra A⊗_k K. The underlying commutative unital k-algebra scalar-extension construction is identical, with chosen K preserved by source text.

The geometrically-reduced source specializes K to perfect closure k^perf; that is an extra field choice within the same general K-algebra scalar extension A⊗_k K used by the geometrically-regular source. The perfect-closure test is not replaced by an arbitrary-extension assertion.

The geometrically-connected source forms A⊗_k K with the canonical unital K-algebra multiplication and structure map. This is the same scalar-extension prerequisite as the geometrically-regular source, with connectedness of Spec(A⊗_k K) an additional requirement.

The matrix-rank source uses free modules R^m and R^n of finite ranks. The finite-presentation source provides the general finite-rank free module R^n notion, with rank variable and basis; this is the same prerequisite, not arbitrary projectivity.

Lazard's characterization states a filtered colimit of finite-rank free R-modules. These are instances of the R^n finite-rank free module used in the finite-module presentation sources; filtered colimit is an additional construction, not part of the prerequisite.

Finite presentation of a module invokes two finite free modules R^m and R^n. They are a pair of instances of the common finite-rank free R-module prerequisite; the exact-sequence relation between them remains source-specific.

The representable-functor source uses the Hom-collection Hom_C(X,Y), and the finitely presentable object source uses Hom_C(X,M_i). Both are precisely collections of arrows with fixed domain X and variable codomain; set-valuedness is a separate local-smallness constraint preserved in the source contexts.

A total order on a field's underlying set F is the same general set-theoretic linear order as an order on S; compatibility with field addition or positivity of products is a further ordered-field axiom, not a distinct order relation prerequisite.

The two field-theoretic sources define an embedded subfield closed under inherited field operations and nonzero inverses. E versus F and K versus F are bound ambient field renamings; no algebraic, normal or finite extension hypothesis is implied by being a subfield.

The topological coequalizer and set-valued diagram-colimit sources both use the smallest equivalence relation on a set containing a prescribed collection of ordered pairs. The topological quotient topology and the diagram indexing restrictions are additional source hypotheses, not part of equivalence-relation generation.

The pointwise continuity source separately refers to an open neighborhood U of x in X and V of f(x) in Y. Each is precisely an open subset containing the specified point; codomain versus domain and the function f are source-level parameters, not distinct neighborhood prerequisites.

Bourbaki-proper and universally closed map sources both require that an explicitly given continuous map send every closed subset to a closed subset of the target. Product versus fiber-product base changes are separate source constructions; no Hausdorffness or properness is inferred from the closed-map prerequisite.

The inverse-limit source uses the product of countably indexed R-modules, while the Mittag-Leffler source uses an arbitrary indexed product. Both are the direct-product module construction with coordinatewise operations; the countable indexing and inverse-limit compatibility equations remain source-specific.

Rank of a linear transformation uses dim_K(im T) for a finite-dimensional image, a direct instance of vector-space dimension as basis cardinality. Finite dimensionality is a separate hypothesis in the rank statement and is not removed.

The integrality-of-element and integral-ring-map formulations both require a monic polynomial whose coefficients originate in R and whose evaluation in S vanishes. Saying 'coefficients in the image of R' is equivalent to evaluating a monic R[T]-polynomial under R→S; injectivity of R→S is not assumed.

The prime-ideal and Noetherian-module sources both refer to an associative commutative coefficient ring with identity. R versus A are bound variable renamings; module Noetherianity and primality impose separate restrictions not part of the ring axioms.

A free module over a localized unital coefficient ring R_{f_i} is the same free-module construction over a particular base ring as the general free R-module prerequisite. Both allow arbitrary basis rank; requiring local freeness on an open cover is a distinct source-level constraint.

Both original statements use the same finite-rank free R-module R^n: the finite projective module source states M is a direct summand of R^n; the finitely presented and Lazard sources use finite free modules. Their common prerequisite is the standard finite direct sum R⊕⋯⊕R with n≥0; projectivity, presentation and flatness are conditions on their separate parent statements.

The abelian category statement calls its canonical Coim(f)→Im(f) arrow an isomorphism; the groupoid statement defines an isomorphism by a two-sided inverse g with gf=id and fg=id. Both use precisely the general categorical isomorphism notion. The abelian-category hypotheses and source-specific canonical comparison are not assimilated into the prerequisite.

Both subspace-topology variants explicitly form τ_A={A∩U:U∈τ}; the shared prerequisite A∩U is binary set intersection. The general variant allows A=∅ and the alternate source excludes empty subspaces; that parent-space convention remains in the original formulation and is not a property of intersection.

The convergent-real-series source starts with a real sequence (a_n) indexed by n≥0, while the power-series and ordinary-generating-function sources use a real coefficient sequence over the same indices. All require a function ℕ_0→ℝ as the shared prerequisite; convergence or a centered formal series is an extra parent-statement condition.

The representable-presheaf statement sets h_U(X)=Hom_C(X,U) for a category with set-valued hom-collections; the preadditive-category statement supplies abelian-group structures on Hom_C(X,Y). Their common prerequisite is a hom-set of arrows with specified domain/codomain; preadditive structure and contravariant precomposition are distinct parent conditions.

The linear-kernel source explicitly identifies ker T with T^{-1}({0_W}). This is the inverse image of a singleton under an arbitrary function, already covered by the canonical general preimage f^{-1}[B]; linearity and use of the zero vector specify the parent kernel statement, not a new inverse-image operation.

The preadditive cokernel requires p∘f=0 and the preadditive kernel requires f∘i=0, each zero being the additive identity in the appropriate Hom abelian group. They share the typed zero-morphism construction, even though the arrow compositions and respective universal properties are different parent conditions.

The uniformizer source tests whether (π) equals a discrete valuation ring's maximal ideal, while the principal-ideal-domain and prime-element sources use an ideal generated by one element. In all cases (a)={ra:r∈R} is the shared principal-ideal prerequisite; maximality, primality and DVR hypotheses stay in their original formulations.

The Cohen-ring source says the maximal ideal is generated by a prime integer p, hence is the principal ideal (p). The prime-element and principal-ideal-domain sources use the same one-generator ideal construction. Being the image of a prime integer and generating the unique maximal ideal are additional source-specific conditions, not new principal-ideal definitions.

The scheme source says each point has a neighborhood isomorphic to Spec(R) with its structure sheaf; the affine-scheme source is a locally ringed space isomorphic to Spec(R) with that same structure sheaf. Both use the canonical ringed-space sheaf O_Spec(R), locally represented on distinguished opens D(f) by R_f; locality of affine charts remains specific to the scheme definition.

The filtered-colimit-of-étale-algebras source uses an R-algebra isomorphism A≅colim A_i; the finite-presentation source uses R-algebra isomorphism with a polynomial quotient. Both require an invertible unital homomorphism commuting with structure maps from R. Étaleness, filteredness and the selected codomain are properties of the parent statements, not of the isomorphism prerequisite.

The essentially-finite-type ring map source says S is R-isomorphic to a localization T^{-1}A; the finite-presentation source says S is R-isomorphic to a finite polynomial quotient. Both employ the same isomorphism notion in the category of unital R-algebras. Localizing, finite generation and quotient presentation stay as separate source hypotheses.

The affine-hull intersection variant takes the intersection of all affine-closed supersets of S, and the topological-closure variant takes the intersection of all topologically closed supersets of A. Their shared prerequisite is the arbitrary intersection of a family of subsets of a fixed universe; the different closure predicates determine distinct indexing families in the parent definitions.

Both discrete-martingale variants require equality of conditional-expectation and process random variables P-almost surely rather than pointwise. One quantifies over adjacent indices n,n+1; the other over all n≤m. Their common missing prerequisite is almost-sure equality of two real random variables; the different quantifier ranges and martingale identities remain distinct mathematical parent formulations.

The locally-nilpotent-ideal and Jacobson-ring sources use commutative rings with multiplicative identity, just as the prime-ideal and Noetherian-module sources explicitly do. They share the associative commutative unital coefficient-ring prerequisite. Nilpotence, radical-ideal and Noetherian module restrictions remain separately attached to their parent statements.

The division-ring source requires a nonzero associative unital ring D and therefore names its two-sided identity 1_D; the unit-of-ring source uses the same two-sided multiplicative identity 1_R in a general associative unital ring. The additional 1_D≠0 restriction follows from the nonzero division-ring parent hypothesis, not a different definition of multiplicative identity.

The categorical-compactness formulation writes Hom_C(X,M_i), and the preadditive and representable-presheaf formulations write Hom_C(X,Y). The prerequisite is the collection of C-arrows with fixed endpoints. Compactness uses set-valued Hom and may need its local-smallness or universe convention, retained in the parent formulation rather than imposed on the underlying Hom-collection.

The category-fibred-in-sets formulation and the category-fibred-in-setoids formulation use exactly the same fibre category E_U: objects e of E with p(e)=U and morphisms whose p-image is id_U. Whether the fibre is discrete or a setoid is an additional distinct restriction in the two parent definitions.

A system of parameters generates an m-primary ideal, and an ideal of definition of a Noetherian local ring is equivalently an ideal with radical m. Within the stated Noetherian local context sqrt(I)=m implies I is m-primary; the common prerequisite is the m-primary-ideal predicate, not equivalence of the two different parent concepts.

The finitely presented ring-map source writes S≅R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m). This invokes the general quotient-ring operation of a commutative unital ring by an ideal, specialized to a polynomial algebra and finitely generated relation ideal; those polynomial and finite-presentation requirements remain parent-specific.

The global-complete-intersection-algebra source presents S as k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c). It invokes the same quotient-ring construction using ideal cosets and inherited ring operations; polynomial variables, finite relations, dimension equality and complete-intersection hypotheses are separately retained in the parent mathematical statement.

The relative-global-complete-intersection source forms R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c), another instance of the general commutative ring quotient A/I. Only the quotient-ring prerequisite is shared; the specified coefficient ring, finitely generated polynomial relations and fibre-dimension constraints remain part of the original parent formulation.

An irreducible component V(p) for a prime p is a Zariski closed set in Spec(R) of the form V(I), here I=p; the support-of-a-finite-module statement also uses Zariski closed subsets V(I). Closedness of subsets in the prime spectrum is the same prerequisite, while minimality of p and the module-annihilator formula stay with their respective parent definitions.

Formally smooth and formally unramified ring-map statements both ask about lifting an R-algebra homomorphism f:S→A/I along the quotient q:A→A/I, i.e. g:S→A with q∘g=f. Smoothness requests existence, unramifiedness at-most-one; neither asserts both. This consolidates only the ordinary algebra-map-lift prerequisite.

Formal smoothness for K/k uses a k-algebra map K→A/I and a k-algebra lift K→A; this is precisely the ordinary R-algebra lifting diagram when R=k and S=K. Both source statements separately require square-zero ideals; uniqueness/existence, separability and field-extension properties remain distinct parent constraints.

The projective-module summand characterization invokes a binary external direct sum P⊕Q, which is the two-index instance of the general finite-support direct-sum construction ⊕_i M_i of R-modules. The direct-summand isomorphism P⊕Q≅R^(I) is a separate projectivity condition and is not identified with any arbitrary direct sum.

For irreducible components of Spec(R), p is a prime ideal minimal under inclusion among primes; the geometrically irreducible algebra source counts the same minimal prime ideals after scalar extension. The shared prerequisite is minimal prime under inclusion, and no hypotheses about geometrical irreducibility or component uniqueness are transferred.

The filtered-category source requires a pair of parallel arrows u,v:i⇉j that become equal after an outgoing morphism, and the equalizer source starts with parallel f,g:X⇉Y. They both use the same typed notion: two arrows with exactly matching source and target. Subsequent equalizing maps and respective universal properties remain different.

The representable-presheaf-morphism source identifies ξ∈G(U) with a Yoneda natural transformation h_U→G; its prerequisite is an ordinary natural transformation between presheaves, already specified by commuting naturality squares. The Yoneda construction is a distinguished instance, and the fibre-product and representability requirements remain parent-specific.

The connected-limit/colimit source references a diagram with a connected indexing category; the ordinary diagram prerequisite is the functor D:I→C. Its context explicitly takes I small, a source-specific indexing restriction. It does not impose smallness on arbitrary C or identify connected diagrams with general diagrams as parent notions.

Finite limit/colimit sources invoke a diagram F:I→C where the index category has finitely many objects and morphisms. This is the general diagram-as-functor construction, specialized to finite and hence small indexing I; the finite index restriction and target locally-small convention remain source-specific.

The locally-finite-collection statement and local Krull-dimension statement both quantify over an open neighborhood U of a point x: x∈U∈τ. The selection for every point and the finite-family-intersection condition are parent-level; this is not merged with a more general, possibly nonopen neighborhood convention.

The local-complete-intersection algebra definition uses standard principal opens D(g_i) in Spec(S), and the scheme topology uses D(f) in Spec(R). Both are the distinguished Zariski opens D(h)={p:h∉p} of an affine prime spectrum. Covering hypotheses and localizations are separately retained.

Mutual independence and pairwise independence both begin with the same indexed measurable event family (A_i) on one probability space, with A_i in the sigma algebra. They differ in the finite-intersection versus pairwise product equations, which remain attached to the parent independence notions, not the event-family prerequisite.

The projective-summand source uses R^(I) as a free module of finitely supported functions on I, and the free-resolution source uses arbitrary-rank free modules F_i. Both require the same free R-module with a basis, equivalently a direct sum of copies of R; the free resolution and summand properties remain separate.

The general random-variable source describes X:(Ω,F)→(S,Σ_S) as measurable iff inverse images of Σ_S sets belong to F; the pushforward-measure source uses the same condition for f:(X,Σ)→(Y,T). They share measurable-map semantics; the probability-measure requirement, measure pushforward, and naming as a random variable are separate parent context.

The tensor comparison in Mittag-Leffler modules uses ∏_i Q_i, the unrestricted product of a family of R-modules; the inverse-limit source uses an instance of this arbitrary product for a countable system. Coordinates, product operations and infinite supports agree. Tensor injectivity and inverse-limit compatibility remain separate parent constraints.

The rational absolute-value source and the strictly-positive-rational source each invoke the usual total order on Q, compatible with rational addition and multiplication by positive elements. The strict-positivity predicate and absolute-value piecewise formula are distinct parent definitions; their ordering prerequisite is identical.

The quasi-separated and separated morphism sources use the identical relative diagonal Δ_{X/S}:X→X×_S X, characterized by both compositions with fibre-product projections being id_X. Quasi-compactness of that diagonal and closed immersion of that diagonal are distinct additional hypotheses retained separately.

The K_0 source uses isomorphism classes of finite projective R-modules and the K'_0 source uses isomorphism classes of finitely generated R-modules. The common prerequisite is module isomorphism equivalence under invertible R-linear maps, restricted to different classes of modules in the source; no equality of those two K-groups follows.

The simple undirected graph and loopless undirected multigraph sources both describe an individual edge by an unordered two-element vertex subset {u,v} with u≠v. Multiplicity of those subsets in the multigraph, versus unique edge membership in the simple graph, is separately preserved in the parent definitions.

The convex-hull intersection formulation computes ⋂ over all convex supersets of U and the topological-closure intersection formulation computes ⋂ over all topologically closed supersets of A. Both invoke arbitrary intersection of a family of subsets; convexity and topological closedness define different indexing predicates retained in their parents.

The full outer measure source codomain and the nonnegative measure source codomain are exactly the extended nonnegative reals [0,+∞], with usual ordering and extended sums. The outer-measure domain P(X) and countable subadditivity differ from measure domain Σ and countable additivity; only the codomain prerequisite is shared.

The finite locally free module and locally free module definitions both require a cover Spec(R)=⋃_i D(f_i) by distinguished principal opens D(f_i). The additional finite-rank restriction on localized modules is parent-level and is not promoted into the general definition of a standard-open cover.

The projective flat Mittag-Leffler criterion uses a direct sum ⊕_i M_i of countably generated modules; the colimit construction uses a direct sum of general R-modules. The shared prerequisite is finite-support direct sum. Countable generation of each summand and global projectivity criteria remain distinct conditions in the parent statement.

The category-hom-set source identifies Hom_C(x,y) for fixed endpoints and explicitly has a small-category size convention; the general preadditive/representable-presheaf source identifies the Hom-collection with the same typing. Smallness grants the set property locally, while the shared prerequisite is precisely the collection of morphisms with fixed endpoints.

The exact-sequence source requires arrows with matching source/target for consecutive compositions, and the epimorphism source requires composability a∘f and b∘f. The shared prerequisite is typed categorical composability, not exactness or epimorphism cancellation.

The independence-of-events formula P(A∩B) and the subspace-topology formula τ_A={A∩U} use the same binary set intersection. The measurable-event and open-subspace restrictions belong to their parents; the underlying intersection is not a new mathematical object.

The nil-ideal formulation invokes the property that each element has some positive power zero, exactly the nilpotence predicate in the reduced-ring formulation. Its commutative-ring assumption specializes the general associative-ring nilpotence prerequisite; 'locally nilpotent ideal' remains its own parent context.

Ordinary and exponential generating functions both define a real power-series domain D as the set of real z where the coefficient-weighted series converges. The coefficients differ (a_n versus a_n/n!), so the actual domains need not agree, but the power-series convergence-domain construction is the same prerequisite.

Splitting fields and irreducible-polynomial quotient fields each use a root α of a polynomial over a smaller field in an extension, meaning polynomial evaluation equals zero. Root multiplicity, splitting and field generation remain parent-specific.

The fibred-setoid and fibred-set 2-category formulations both define 2-morphisms as natural transformations of over-base functors whose components lie over identity arrows in C. Whether a fibre is a setoid or discrete is a distinct parent constraint.

Integral-element and integral-ring-map formulations use a monic polynomial to test vanishing at an element; standard étale maps and minimal polynomials also use the leading-coefficient-one predicate. The common prerequisite is being monic; satisfaction of a monic equation or étaleness is not identified.

Orthogonal-polynomial integrals over (a,b) and antiderivatives on open real interval I both invoke an open connected real interval as domain. Bounded and unbounded endpoint choices specialize that concept; orthogonality and differentiability remain separate.

Both independent smooth-ring-map formulations invoke chain-complex quasi-isomorphism: a chain map inducing homology isomorphisms or a zigzag in derived comparisons. Finite projectivity of the comparison module and the cotangent-complex construction are parent-level conditions.

The two affine-hull variants invoke exactly finite affine combinations ∑α_i x_i with real scalar coefficients summing to one, without nonnegativity. The hull's intersection-of-affine-closed-sets versus generating-set presentation are distinct equivalent parent formulations and should not be conflated with convex combinations.

Both congruence-modulo-m variants for integers use m|(a−b), or existence of k∈ℤ with a−b=km; one emphasizes m>0 and the other m≠0. The common prerequisite is integer divisibility; positive-modulus convention stays parent-specific.

Locally uniform convergence and local quasi-compactness both quantify over general neighborhoods containing an open neighborhood of x, which need not themselves be open. Their respective uniformity and compactness conditions remain parent-level; do not merge these neighborhoods with the stricter open-neighborhood identity.

The constructible-spectrum formulation uses the distinguished open D(f)={p:f∉p}, just as the Zariski-scheme topology and local complete-intersection formulations. These are the same principal Zariski-open prerequisite, with constructible Boolean operations and covering conditions retained in parents.

Local section gluing over standard D(f_i) and the Zariski-topology definition use the same distinguished prime-spectrum open D(f), where f_i is a specialized generator. Pairwise intersections D(f_i f_j), unit-ideal cover and gluing are additional parent conditions.

Scheme morphisms and morphisms of locally ringed spaces require the same local-homomorphism condition on stalk maps O_{Y,f(x)}→O_{X,x}, preserving maximal ideals by inverse image. Scheme-specific global sheaf compatibility is a separate parent condition.

The scheme fibre product and categorical pullback definitions both first require a commuting cone P→X,P→Y over X→S←Y, with equal composites. The universal property and particular scheme category remain separate; this merges only the typed compatible-cone prerequisite.

Real-time and discrete-time martingale formulations invoke equality of two random variables outside a null set. Conditional expectation, real/discrete index sets and filtration-adaptation requirements are parent-specific, while equality P(X≠Y)=0 is shared.

The (2,1)-categorical fibre-product source requires an invertible comparison 2-cell, and the strict 2-category equivalence source requires vertically invertible 2-morphisms. They share the two-sided 2-cell inverse prerequisite, with the (2,1) hypothesis and pseudocone context kept separate.

The Grothendieck construction of a strict groupoid-valued presheaf C^op→Groupoids is an instance of the Grothendieck construction of a category-valued presheaf C^op→Cat. Groupoid fibres and the split-fibred-in-groupoids hypothesis are parent-specific; the total category-of-elements construction is shared.

The standard étale source asserts an R-algebra isomorphism S≅R[x]_g/(f), and the filtered-colimit / finite-type sources invoke the same invertible unital R-algebra homomorphism notion. Monic f, localization g, derivatives and étaleness are retained separately.

The 'scheme' source and 'affine scheme' source both invoke isomorphism of locally ringed spaces, meaning a two-sided inverse among morphisms preserving stalk-local ring structure. Scheme, affine and sheaf-local hypotheses remain in their parent definitions.

The topological boundary expression cl_X(A)\int_X(A) uses the same relative set complement C\I as the sigma-algebra difference axiom A\B. Closure and interior are independently typed sources and not transferred into set difference.

The constructible-set source uses U\V for retrocompact open U,V, an instance of the binary set difference A\B in the sigma-algebra source. Retrocompactness and openness are extra parent hypotheses, not generic properties of difference.

The boundary formula's X\A is the relative complement of A in ambient set X, a special case of A\B. The ambient X and subsequent topological closure remain source-specific; no identification is made between complement and closure.

Noetherian modules and Noetherian rings both invoke existence of an inclusion-maximal member of every nonempty poset family of respectively submodules or ideals. The abstract maximal-versus-greatest predicate is the same; the eligible family type and Noetherian properties are not identical.

The convex-set source uses a two-point convex combination tx+(1−t)y for t∈[0,1], which is an instance of the finite convex-combination construction in the convex-hull source. Terms with zero weights can be removed or replaced by a single coefficient 1; positivity convention and arity are specialized, not new operations.

Both normal-extension formulations use the same polynomial splitting condition: over a field extension, a nonzero polynomial is a scalar multiple of linear factors, with multiplicities. One ranges over irreducibles with roots and the other over element minimal polynomials; normality itself stays parent-level.

A countable union of pairwise disjoint members used in an equivalent sigma-algebra axiom is a countable indexed union of sets, exactly the prerequisite used in the ordinary sigma-algebra formulation. Pairwise-disjointness and closure under that union are separate source-specific conditions.

The outer-measure codomain record and the general nonnegative-measure codomain record denote the same extended nonnegative reals [0,+∞], with infinity included and standard extended addition/order. Countable subadditivity versus additivity is a parent distinction.

The category localization source requests invertibility of a morphism, defined by existence of an inverse g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y. This is precisely the categorical-isomorphism prerequisite already used in groupoids; universal localization is a distinct parent.

The functor-of-points source's Hom_Sch(T,X) is the hom-collection of morphisms with fixed source and target in the locally small category of schemes. It is an instance of Hom_C(A,B) under C=Sch; contravariance and pullback by precomposition remain source-specific.

The bounded-operator norm source takes sup of the set {||Tx||:||x||≤1}; the Dedekind completeness source defines least upper bound sup(A) in an ordered set. The operator-norm supremum is a special bounded nonempty real-set instance, not a distinct supremum predicate.

The covariant representability source invokes F:C→Sets, an ordinary covariant functor into the category of sets, which is an instance of the generic functor F:C→D. Its set-valuedness and any local-smallness convention remain parent-specific; generic functorial identity/composition laws are the shared prerequisite.

Local module descent uses a finite principal Zariski cover Spec(R)=⋃_iD(f_i); locally free modules use an arbitrary family of standard opens covering Spec(R). The cover-by-principal-opens construction is shared; source's finite index restriction, unit-ideal generator equivalence and gluing conditions stay parent-specific.

The faithfully flat and flat ring-map definitions both equip S with precisely the restriction-of-scalars R-module structure induced by φ:R→S, with r·s=φ(r)s. Faithful flatness and flatness are different parent properties, not equivalent to the module action itself.

The unital and nonunital Boolean-ring formulations both require universal elementwise idempotence x²=x. The two raw candidate contexts literally match on the underlying idempotent predicate. Having a unit remains a separate parent ring convention, not conferred by idempotence.

The Nagata-ring source uses the quotient R/p by a prime ideal p. This is the general commutative unital quotient-ring operation R/I specialized to I=p; primality and Japanese/Nagata conditions remain specific to the source.

The geometrically reduced base-change formulation and geometrically integral/perfect-closure formulations invoke identical scalar extension of commutative unital k-algebras along K/k, forming A⊗_kK as a K-algebra with induced multiplication. Reducedness, integrality and choice of K are distinct parent requirements.

The finite-field and prime-field characteristic sources both use a prime positive integer p>1, whose only positive divisors are 1 and p; this is ordinary integer primality, not the different notions of prime ideal or prime-power cardinality.

The clopen-spectrum source's D(e) is the distinguished principal open D(f) of Spec(R) specialized to an idempotent element e. Idempotence makes this open also closed but must remain a source-specific additional hypothesis.

Nonnegatively graded rings and ℤ-graded modules both use an internal additive-group direct-sum decomposition with unique finitely supported homogeneous components. Nonnegative-versus-integer index grading and multiplication/module compatibility are separate parent-specific data.

Both the component-union classification of Spec(R) and the clopen-spectrum classification invoke the same idempotent ring element e∈R satisfying e²=e. An ideal generated by idempotents and a single clopen idempotent are distinct higher constructions; the shared prerequisite is exactly elementwise idempotency.

The connected-space and connected-topological-space variants both refer to a subset of a fixed topological space simultaneously open and closed in that ambient topology. The parent connectedness statements differ on whether the empty space is admitted; clopen does not resolve that discrepancy.

Hausdorff separation invokes open neighborhoods of distinct points, and the continuity pointwise criterion invokes open neighborhoods of image and source points. The common prerequisite is an open subset containing a specified point; ordinary neighborhoods that merely contain an open subset remain distinct.

The nilpotent-ideal source uses the positive integral ideal power I^n, and pure-ideal/completion sources use ideal multiplication IJ and its iterations I^n. Both depend on ordinary ideal multiplication in a ring, while the choice of n and nilpotence equation I^n=0 are parent hypotheses.

Finite locally free modules use M_f≅R_f^n over the localized ring R_f, and the filtered-colimit/presentation sources use finite-rank free R-modules R^n. They share finite free rank-n module construction over a unital base ring; localized base and rank varying with chart are parent-specific.

Topological separatedness requires X×_Y X, the self-pullback of f:X→Y. Universally closed continuous maps require X×_Y Z, an ordinary topological pullback. The first is the specialization Z=X with both arrows f; the subspace-topology pullback construction is identical, but diagonal closedness and universal closedness remain distinct.

An element integral over an ideal is tested by a positive-degree monic polynomial P(T), and étale/minimal-polynomial definitions use a univariate polynomial with leading coefficient 1. The monic predicate is shared; positive degree and coefficient conditions a_j∈I^{d-j} stay parent-specific.

The universally closed topological map and universally closed scheme morphism definitions each invoke that a particular continuous base-change map sends closed subsets to closed subsets. That is the same closed-map prerequisite; schemes vs arbitrary topological spaces and universal quantification over base changes remain parent-specific.

Discrete-time and real-time martingale definitions both use L^1 integrability of each real random variable, E|X_t|<∞; the index symbol and its range (natural vs nonnegative real time) do not alter the integrability predicate. Filtration and martingale equalities remain separate.

Topological closure and irreducible-space sources both require F closed in X exactly when X\F is open in its topology. Neither assumes a metric or Hausdorff space, so these are identical general closed-subset prerequisites, distinct from a closed map or closed immersion.

The topological boundary formula cl_X(A)∩cl_X(X\A) and subspace topology A∩U are instances of the same binary intersection of arbitrary sets. Closure, complement and openness are separate input restrictions of their parent formulas, not properties of the binary intersection operation.

The Rees algebra source forms ⊕_{n≥0}I^n, where each ideal power is an R-module and the direct sum is finite-support external module sum. The generic module-colimit source defines ⊕_iM_i in precisely that manner. Graded multiplication and the ideal-power indexing are additional Rees-algebra structure.

The tensor algebra source forms the external direct sum of its tensor powers M^{⊗n}, which are R-modules. It shares the finite-support module direct-sum construction ⊕_i M_i; tensor powers and concatenation multiplication remain parent-specific.

The irreducible-component definition picks an inclusion-maximal irreducible subset among all irreducible subsets of X. The Noetherian ideal/module sources use the same order-theoretic maximal-member predicate in families ordered by inclusion. Irreducibility and Noetherianity are distinct properties.

Formal smoothness uses an R-algebra A with quotient A/I and canonical algebra map A→A/I for a square-zero ideal I. This contains the ordinary ring quotient construction, already used for I-adic and polynomial quotients. The R-algebra action, I²=0 and the lifting test remain source-specific.

Algebraicity of a field extension invokes a univariate k-polynomial f(T); the general indexed R-polynomial algebra includes the one-variable polynomial ring with R=k. Evaluation at α and nonzero-polynomial requirements are additional parent conditions, not automatically part of the polynomial-ring prerequisite.

The algebraic-extension source selects a nonzero polynomial P∈F[T], which is an element of the one-variable polynomial ring over F. The general indexed polynomial-algebra construction includes this case; the nonzero predicate and existence of a root are retained in the parent definition.

The strongly transcendental source forms finite coefficient polynomial expressions a_0+...+a_n x^n under R⊆S, using the one-variable polynomial-algebra structure over R before evaluation at x∈S. The ambient polynomial ring is the shared prerequisite; evaluation and annihilator implications remain separate.

The affine quasi-coherent sheaf source and the Zariski topology/constructible sources invoke exactly distinguished principal opens D(f) of Spec(R). The localization-of-sections theorem and covers by those opens remain different parent conditions.

A closed immersion of locally ringed spaces asks for a locally section-generated kernel ideal sheaf ker(O_X→i_*O_Z). This is an instance of a locally section-generated ideal subsheaf I⊆O_X used in closed-subspace construction; being specifically a kernel and the immersion's topological conditions remain parent-specific.

The Hausdorff diagonal characterization asks that Δ_X be closed in the product-topology space X×X. This is the general topological closed-subset predicate that an ambient complement is open, specialized to the ambient product; Hausdorffness and diagonality stay parent-specific.

Conditional expectation requires integrable real X and Z, namely E|X|<∞ and E|Z|<∞. Continuous-time and discrete-time martingale formulations require exactly the L¹ integrability predicate for each real random variable X_t. Time indexing and conditional-expectation criteria stay parent-specific.

The one-variable derivative uses [f(a+h)-f(a)]/h with h→0 and h≠0. The directional derivative uses [f(a+tu)-f(a)]/t, specializing in one dimension and direction u=1 to the same finite-difference quotient. The direction vector and Euclidean dimension stay parent-specific.

Finite-indexed intersection ⋂_{j∈J}A_j in joint independence is an iterated instance of ordinary set intersection of arbitrary subsets, used in topology and binary independence. Empty-family convention Ω and finite indexing remain parent-specific, not intrinsic to binary intersection.

Continuous weighted moments ∫_a^b|x|^k w(x)dx are absolute moments ∫|x|^k dμ for measure dμ=w(x)1_(a,b)(x)dx. The finite-moment construction agrees while interval, density and support hypotheses remain parent-specific.

Finite positive-weight orthogonality Σ_{x∈X}p_n(x)p_m(x)w_x=0 uses the same discrete weighted inner-product equation as countably infinite support. In the finite case convergence is automatic; infinite support and moment assumptions are parent-specific.

Intermediate subfield k⊆L⊆K is an ordinary subfield L of K with inherited operations, together with the additional lower inclusion of k. This shares the subfield prerequisite in extension/prime-subfield sources, not the parent intermediate-field containment or algebraicity.

The coefficient-ring source uses pΛ, the principal ideal of Λ generated by the image of integer p. The general principal ideal (p) in a ring is exactly the same generated-ideal construction, while residue-characteristic and maximal-ideal intersection remain parent-specific.

The nonzero commutative unital ring R has associative commutative multiplication and a specified identity, exactly the general commutative unital ring prerequisite. Nonzeroness 0≠1 and field inversion, when present, remain parent-specific rather than imposed on all unital rings.

The geometric-irreducibility source uses A⊗_k K for a commutative unital k-algebra A and field extension K/k. Five geometrically reduced/connected/regular source contexts use R⊗_k K with precisely the same K-algebra multiplication (a⊗x)(b⊗y)=ab⊗xy. A versus R is a bound-variable name, not a new construction; geometric predicates and quantifiers over K stay parent-specific.

Splitting-field source requires a polynomial P to factor completely into linear factors over E. Normal algebraic extension sources require a polynomial to split over K as c∏(T−α_j), retaining leading scalar and multiplicities. These are the identical complete-linear-factorization prerequisite. Generation by roots, normality, and irreducibility are distinct parent-only assertions.

The preordered-set formulation demands a reflexive binary relation iRi for every i in I; the independent relation-property formulation uses (x,x)∈R for every x∈S. These are exactly the same quantified reflexivity property of a binary relation. Transitivity, symmetry, antisymmetry, and whether the relation is itself a preorder remain parent-specific.

The connected-component source selects a connected subset C inclusion-maximal among connected subsets of X. That is the ordinary poset definition of maximal element of a specified family of subsets under inclusion: no distinct admissible member properly contains C. The condition that the family consists of connected subsets remains essential and is not promoted to arbitrary maximality; maximal is not greatest or path-connected.

The étale-ring-map source uses H_1(C•)=ker(d_1)/im(d_2) for a naive cotangent chain complex, exactly the i=1 specialization of H_i(C•)=ker(d_i)/im(d_{i+1}) recorded in the Tor-from-free-resolution source. In the two-term complex d_2 has zero source; H_1=0 is an additional vanishing predicate, not part of the general definition of homology.

In the syntomic-ring-map source the fibre algebra S⊗_R κ(p) is the exact base-change commutative R′-algebra construction S⊗_R R′ used in the universal-homeomorphism source, specialized to the R-algebra R′=κ(p). Tensor multiplication, unit and scalar structure agree. Residue field, local complete intersection, flatness and quantification over prime p belong solely to the syntomic parent.

The topological pointwise-convergence source uses the function set T^D={f:D→T}, canonically identical to the set-theoretic Cartesian product ∏_{d∈D}T of a constant indexed family. The product-topology source defines the general indexed Cartesian product ∏_{i∈I}X_i. Topological convergence and coordinate projections are additional parent-specific constructions, not attributes of a bare product set.

The two-category-over-base source defines 2-morphisms as natural transformations between functors over C with components mapping to identity arrows in C. The categories-fibred-in-sets and -setoids sources use the same exact over-base natural transformation, with each component projecting to id_{p(x)}. The separate object types of the total categories remain parent-specific, and no equivalence of the 2-categories is asserted.

For an affine open U in a scheme S, global sections of the restricted structure sheaf O_U have ring Γ(U,O_U)=O_S(U) by the definition of sheaf restriction. The reduced-scheme sectionwise source uses O_X(U) for precisely the same sheaf-section ring construction. Affineness of U and the scheme-cardinality supremum are parent-only restrictions, and neither expression means a stalk.

The separably-generated-extension source's k(B), with B a potentially infinite transcendence basis over k, is a rational-function field in algebraically independent indeterminates B. The purely-transcendental-extension source's k(X_i:i∈I) is the fraction field of the polynomial algebra in an arbitrary indexed independent family, allowing finite expression support. Relabel b↔X_b to obtain the same k-field construction; separability of the subsequent extension and existence of a basis remain source-specific.

Depth source takes the supremum of nonnegative lengths of M-regular sequences contained in an ideal. The underlying order operation is the least upper bound of the set of lengths in the ordered set ℕ∪{∞}, precisely the general poset-supremum construction. The extended value ∞, restriction to M-regular sequences, and containment in I remain defining source-context qualifications.

The finite-module-dimension source takes suprema of lengths of prime chains in Supp_R(M). These are least upper bounds in ℕ∪{∞} just as for any subset of an ordered set, with +∞ for unbounded integer lengths. The prime-chain restriction and support of M are parent-specific and do not become part of the abstract supremum prerequisite.

A finite rank free left R-module R^n is the finite-index direct sum of copies of R and hence the n-element-basis case of the generic free left R-module R^{(I)}. The finite-rank/standard-basis requirements for rank and Lazard, finite-presentation and finite-projective sources remain parent-specific; a free module of arbitrary rank is not assumed finite or locally free by this alias.

The splitting-field source's extension generated by F together with all roots of P in E is the general field-generation construction F(B), taking B to be the subset of roots. The target candidate defines k(B) as the least intermediate subfield containing the base field and B. Full splitting of P, root selection, and splitting-field minimality remain only in the parent construction.

The primitive-element source uses F(α), the smallest subfield containing F and a selected α, which is precisely k(B) for base k=F and singleton generator set B={α}. Rational expressions in α describe that generated subfield; its single-generator restriction and the primitive-element assertion are parent-specific, not imposed on arbitrary generated fields.

A finitely generated intermediate field E=k(a_1,...,a_n) within K is the general generated-subfield k(B) construction for finite generator set B={a_1,...,a_n}. The source's finiteness of B, selected ambient intermediate field, and distinction from finite vector-space degree remain explicit parent-specific qualifications.

The Kummer-extension source uses K(α), a simple field generated from K by adjoining α, which is the general generated-subfield construction k(B) with base k=K and singleton B={α}. The algebraic equation α^n=a, associated hypotheses on roots of unity and Kummer structure are extra conditions of the parent, not consequences of field generation.

The representable-functor-on-schemes source invokes a natural isomorphism of contravariant Set-valued functors; the representable-covariant-functor source invokes a natural isomorphism of covariant Set-valued functors. Both require the identical abstract prerequisite: a natural transformation with natural inverse, equivalently a natural family of isomorphism components. Different domain categories, functor variance and Hom-functor formulas remain attached to their respective sources and are NOT conflated.

The scheme-size source takes a least upper bound of a set of cardinal numbers ordered by cardinal comparison. This shares only the abstract poset supremum construction sup(A) as least upper bound with other ordered-set sources. The ambient order here is the cardinal order (not the ordered reals), the values are cardinals and the result is a cardinal supremum, all retained as source-specific typing; no cardinal/real-value identification is asserted.

The total-quotient-ring source localizes R at the set S of its non-zero-divisors. This S contains 1 and is multiplicatively closed, exactly the general multiplicative-subset prerequisite used by ring/module localization. Requiring S to be all regular elements, rather than an arbitrary multiplicative subset, remains source-specific and is not generalized.

The topology-subbasis source forms finite intersections of open subbasic sets, including the empty finite intersection X. The independent topological-space axiom source uses the identical finite-indexed set-intersection operation with the same empty-index convention. Openness of each member, closure under intersections and basis generation are parent-specific, not intrinsic to a set intersection.

The affine-scheme-fibre-product formulation uses B⊗_A C of two commutative A-algebras, with multiplication (b⊗c)(b′⊗c′)=bb′⊗cc′. The universal-homeomorphism and syntomic sources use S⊗_R R′ with the same multiplication after renaming A=R, B=S, C=R′. This aliases the tensor-product algebra prerequisite only; no fibre-product universal property or homeomorphism/local-CI condition is equated.

The geometrically integral algebra source uses commutative unital scalar extension A⊗_k K for a field extension K/k, with exactly the same tensor-product K-algebra multiplication and canonical scalar structure as the previously consolidated R⊗_k K prerequisite (A and R are variable labels). The geometric integrality test and universal quantifier over K stay parent-specific.

The two independently sourced normal-subgroup formulations use gNg⁻¹={gng⁻¹:n∈N}. When N is a subgroup the conjugate subset is also a subgroup; the elementwise conjugation set operation is identical in both. Subgroup hypotheses, gNg⁻¹⊆N and equality/normality remain with each source, not inferred from arbitrary subset conjugation.

The Dedekind-domain factorization characterization requires a finite iterated product P_1⋯P_n of ideals with the same finite-sums-of-products construction as the binary ideal product IJ, including R as the empty product. The conditions that the factors are nonzero prime ideals, and that factorization is unique, belong only to the Dedekind characterization; aliasing does not make an arbitrary product prime or unique.

The locally-ringed-space definition uses the stalk O_{X,x} at every point x, which is precisely the sheaf-theoretic filtered colimit of sections on neighborhoods used in the reduced-scheme source's stalk prerequisite. Requiring each stalk to be a local ring remains a condition defining locally ringed spaces, not a property of stalks of every sheaf of rings.

The split-fibred-category source uses an isomorphism of categories over C with inverse over C. The split-fibred-groupoid source identifies exactly that category-over-base isomorphism, in both cases strictly commuting with projection functors. Requiring both categories to be fibred, or the chosen Grothendieck construction to be strict, remains parent-specific; ordinary category-over-base isomorphism does not itself imply fibration.

Catenarity uses maximal finite strict chains of irreducible closed subsets between Y⊆Z, which first have exactly the same underlying Z_0⊊⋯⊊Z_n finite strict chain construction and length convention as Krull dimension of a space. The no-intermediate-set maximality condition, fixed endpoints, finite codimension and equality of maximal-chain lengths are extra parent constraints.

The category-fibred-in-sets source invokes the ordinary covariant functor p:E→C from total category to base category without assumed smallness. This is the same general identity/composition-preserving category functor prerequisite as the unrestricted F:C→D used in 2-categories and fibrations; p is merely a variable name. The cartesian-lift and discrete-fibre conditions remain parent-specific and are not imposed on all functors.

The limit/colimit and finite-diagram sources define a diagram F:I→C as an ordinary identity/composition-preserving functor from an indexing category I to an arbitrary target category C, not a small-to-small functor. Thus a diagram's underlying functor is precisely the unrestricted ordinary-functor prerequisite; index finiteness, connectedness, cone structure and universal limit/colimit claims remain parent-specific.

The iso-comma-category source requires two ordinary covariant functors F:A→C and G:B→C, each preserving identities and composition without any smallness restriction. This invokes the general unrestricted ordinary-functor prerequisite twice; their shared codomain, the objects (a,b,α) and the iso-comma compatibility equations remain conditions only of the parent iso-comma construction.

The left-adjoint source uses ordinary functors L:C→D and R:D→C, differing only in domain/codomain orientation and naming from a generic identity/composition-preserving functor. Adjointness, naturality of Hom-bijections, and the fact that L and R have opposite domain assignments are extra parent constraints, not properties of an arbitrary functor.

The two-category-of-fibred-sets source uses functors H:E→E′ of total categories, ordinary functors at the level of objects/arrows, with the additional equation p′H=p. The general unrestricted functor prerequisite is identical while the over-base compatibility and fibration hypotheses remain source-specific and do not follow from ordinary functoriality.

A tensor bifunctor ⊗:C×C→C in a monoidal category is an ordinary covariant functor with source the product category C×C, preserving identities and compositions for pairs of arrows. Its bifunctor notation does not introduce a different functoriality axiom. Product-category construction, tensor object, associator and monoidal coherence remain source-specific and are not collapsed into arbitrary functor meaning.

In the preordered-set source, transitivity of relation ≤ on I is ∀i,j,k (i≤j and j≤k ⇒ i≤k). In the equivalence-relation source, transitivity of ∼ on S is the identical quantified binary-relation property, with only variables and notation renamed. Reflexivity, symmetry and all preorder/equivalence requirements stay parent-specific and are not implied by transitivity alone.

The presheaf-fibre-product source requires two natural transformations F⇒G and H⇒G between contravariant set-valued presheaves, with component maps compatible with restriction. The representable-presheaf-morphism source requires exactly the same natural-transformation prerequisite for one map. Two-arrow multiplicity, common target G, fibre product and representability conditions remain parent-specific.

The unital-ring-homomorphism source stipulates R and S are each associative rings with a specified multiplicative identity. Each individually has the exact unital ring structure also used in the unital Boolean-ring source. The existence of two rings and the additional equation φ(1_R)=1_S are constraints of the homomorphism source; they are not part of the definition of one unital ring.

The compatible-localized-sections source requires finite elements f_i to generate the entire unital ring R, equivalently (f_1,...,f_n)=R and a linear combination Σ r_i f_i=1. The relatively-prime-polynomial source uses the identical unit ideal (1)=R, specialized to R=k[x]. Their shared prerequisite is the unit ideal; the finite-generation equality and number of generators remain parent-specific conditions.

In the finite-module support and irreducible-component sources, a Zariski-closed subset of Spec(R) has the form V(I)={p in Spec(R): I⊆p}. This is exactly the Zariski vanishing-locus construction V(I) used to define closed sets in the ring-spectrum source. The particular ideal Ann_R(M), Noetherian hypotheses, and irreducible-component condition remain parent-specific.

The constructible-subset-on-affine-spectrum source's V(g_1,...,g_m) consists of primes containing every g_i, identically V((g_1,...,g_m)), the ordinary Zariski-closed-locus V(I) for the finitely generated ideal I. The number of generators, accompanying distinguished open D(f), and finite-union constructibility clause remain the parent's extra structure.

The relative-dimension-at-a-prime source says q in Spec(S) lies over p in Spec(R) for R→S exactly when p is the inverse-image contraction φ^{-1}(q). The relative-assassin source explicitly uses that same contracted prime construction p=q∩R (shorthand along the structure map). Relative dimension, local fibre topology, and associated-prime requirements are separate parent-specific data.

The sigma-algebra source's complement X\A is the general relative set difference A\B specialized to the first set X, the ambient universe. Both definitions use the operation {x in first set : x not in second set}. Measurability, the ambient universe restriction, and the topological-boundary or constructible-set uses remain parent-specific; the alias is for the underlying set-difference prerequisite.

The locally-ringed-space morphism source's compatible structure-sheaf morphism for continuous f:X→Y is the ordinary ring-sheaf map O_Y→f_*O_X, equivalently via sheaf adjunction f^{-1}O_Y→O_X, as stated in the scheme-morphism source. Requiring induced stalk maps to be local homomorphisms and requiring the spaces to be schemes are separate parent conditions.

The closed-immersion source uses a sheaf-ring homomorphism O_X→i_*O_Z induced by continuous i:Z→X, exactly the general compatible structure-sheaf morphism O_Y→f_*O_X used for a scheme morphism after renaming f=i, Y=X, source X=Z. The surjectivity of this map, the direct-image sheaf on a closed subset, its locally section-generated kernel, and the closed underlying homeomorphism are extra parent conditions, not properties of a general sheaf homomorphism.

The independent-random-variables source defines σ(X_n) as the collection of measurable inverse-image sets X_n^{-1}(B), B∈Σ_S. This collection is already a σ-algebra, hence it is exactly the smallest σ-algebra containing that family of inverse images: an instance of the general σ-algebra generated by a chosen family. The special choice of inverse images, measurability, and mutual independence of multiple σ-algebras remain parent-specific and are not collapsed into the Borel topological case τ.

The going-up and going-down formulations' statement that a prime q of S lies above p of R under φ:R→S means φ^{-1}(q)=p, exactly the same prime-contraction operation underlying the relative-dimension and relative-assassin source contexts. Going up/down assert additional EXISTENCE of compatible prime ideals in chains and remain separate parent predicates.

Locally finite families and local Krull dimension take an open neighbourhood U of x, namely x∈U∈τ_X. This is exactly the open-neighborhood predicate already used for Hausdorff spaces and pointwise continuity, with British/American spellings only. No weaker arbitrary neighborhood notion is conflated: that broader concept remains missing. The finiteness and local-dimension conditions stay with their parent formulations.

The split-fibred-category source posits a base category C without a smallness hypothesis. Its prerequisite is the same ordinary category with objects, arrows, associative composition and identities as the size-unrestricted canonical candidate. The extra cleavage/splitting and Grothendieck construction are source-specific and no small-category condition is imported.

The categorical-fibre-product source requires an ordinary category possessing objects/arrows and composition, with no bound on its object collection. Its 'category and arrows' prerequisite is precisely the generic size-unrestricted category concept; existence and universal properties of this particular fibre product remain the parent meaning, not implied by category alone.

The filtered-category source starts with an arbitrary category I of objects, morphisms and their compositions; the displayed axioms make I nonempty and filtered but do not demand smallness. This is the ordinary size-unrestricted category prerequisite. Filteredness, nonemptiness and parallel-arrow equalization are parent conditions and not inferred for any general category.

The categorical-limit and colimit source formulas use index category I and target category C, each with objects, arrows, identity and associative composition. They do not stipulate a small target category. This is the size-unrestricted underlying ordinary-category prerequisite, instantiated twice; the diagram functor, cone/cocone and universal properties remain additional parent conditions.

In flat and faithfully flat module definitions, the operation N↦N⊗_R M, with morphism action f↦f⊗id_M, is a covariant functor between the categories of R-modules, preserving identities and composition and with no small-category hypothesis. This uses the same generic functor prerequisite; the tensor-product implementation and (reflection and) preservation of exactness are additional parent-specific requirements.

The projective-module Hom exactness source's covariant Hom_R(P,−) takes an R-module N to Hom_R(P,N) and a morphism g to postcomposition g∘−, preserving identities and compositions. Thus it is a typed instance of unrestricted ordinary functoriality. The choice of Hom construction, additivity, and exactness condition remain attached to the projectivity source, and no restriction to small categories is imported.

The short-exact-sequence source explicitly uses the symbols 0→A→B→C→0 in an abelian category, where 0 denotes the zero object (both initial and terminal). The additive-category source likewise requires a zero object, both initial and terminal. These are the same underlying categorical prerequisite; exactness, images, kernels and individual sequence arrows stay with the parent source.

The representable presheaf h_U acts on g:Y→X by precomposition Hom_C(X,U)→Hom_C(Y,U), f↦f∘g. The functor-of-points h_X acts on α:T′→T by the identical precomposition operation Hom(T,X)→Hom(T′,X), h↦h∘α. Objects differ but the categorical prerequisite is the same operation preserving identities and composition. The representability, scheme and contravariance data remain source-specific.

The independently sourced proper vertex k-coloring formulations both use the exactly specified label set {1,…,k} for integer k≥1 as the color codomain. The provisional formula explicitly states that c need not be surjective and the screened formula has the same c:V→{1,…,k} convention; both prerequisites denote the same finite label palette, not the proper-coloring constraint itself.

The affine fibre-product source asserts a canonical isomorphism of schemes over Spec(A), and the affine closed-subscheme source asserts an isomorphism of schemes over Spec(R). In both, an S-scheme isomorphism is an invertible scheme morphism whose forward and inverse maps commute with the fixed structural maps to S; A/R are dummy coefficient-ring variables. The fibre-product tensor construction and closed immersion remain separate mathematical parent conditions.

The two provisional affine-hull formulations define or characterize aff(S) in R^d using the finite affine combination Σ_{i=1}^k α_i x_i with Σα_i=1 and no positivity constraint. The alternate affine-closed-intersection formulation explicitly requires closure under exactly such combinations. Thus both candidate labels are the same affine-combination prerequisite. The aff(S)=∅ convention for S=∅ belongs to the parent affine-hull variant and is preserved.

The continuous-indexed martingale formulation and the real-time adapted stochastic-process formulation both use the increasing family (F_t)_{t≥0} of σ-algebras for every real t≥0, with F_s⊆F_t whenever s≤t. Their shared prerequisite is a continuous-time filtration, distinct from the separately present discrete-time (F_n) filtration. Martingale conditional expectations and process adaptedness remain source-specific.

In the algebraically closed field source, a root a∈K of a nonconstant polynomial f∈K[x] means f(a)=0. In the irreducible polynomial quotient, splitting-field and separable-degree sources, a root α in a field extension E/F means f(α)=0 after coefficient inclusion. The first is precisely the K=F=E special case of the second polynomial-root prerequisite. Neither is confused with a root of unity or a field radical.

Both candidate identities occur in the SAME provisional trace-of-a-square-matrix source: K is a field, n≥1 and A=(a_ij)∈M_n(K). A square n-by-n matrix over K and a square matrix of finite order n≥1 over K are the identical underlying linear-algebraic prerequisite in this source, not alternative sizes, rings or matrix operations. The diagonal sum defining trace remains separate.

The categorical fibre-product and scheme fibre-product sources each have maps X→S and Y→S and a vertex T or P with maps u:T→X, v:T→Y satisfying fu=gv, i.e. a cone over the cospan-shaped diagram. The generic category-limit source defines a cone on F:I→C by arrows L→F(i) compatible with diagram arrows, with no universality required. Taking I to be the cospan indexing category gives precisely the same underlying cone prerequisite. Pullback universality and the scheme-specific category remain distinct parent conditions; this does not equate arbitrary cones with pullback limits.

The essentially-constant ind-diagram parent invokes maps M_i→X compatible with all transitions of a filtered diagram, without asserting X is the colimit. The generic category-colimit parent defines exactly this compatible family as a cocone F(i)→Q, with I arbitrary and the colimit universal property added separately. The first is an instance using I filtered, F(i)=M_i and Q=X. This is an identity of the underlying cocone prerequisite only, not an identity of filteredness, essential constancy and colimit universality.

The Tor flatness local-criterion source takes a local homomorphism R→S of Noetherian local rings; the locally ringed space and scheme morphism sources require homomorphisms between local stalk rings that are local. In both cases the foundational condition is f^{-1}(m_S)=m_R for the respective maximal ideals. The stronger Noetherian, stalkwise, morphism-of-sheaves and Tor hypotheses remain in their parent texts. Equivalently requiring f(m_R)⊆m_S is valid for unital maps of local rings.

The left R-module kernel parent writes ker(φ)=φ^{-1}({0_N}), explicitly a set-theoretic preimage of the singleton zero under the underlying function φ:M→N, with no invertibility requirement. The existing broadly recurring inverse-image prerequisite defines f^{-1}[B]={x:f(x)∈B} for every function and subset of the codomain. Taking f=φ and B={0_N} identifies the prerequisite exactly; R-linearity, the submodule property and the kernel equation stay parent-specific.

For directed R-module transitions u_ij:M_i→M_j, the source's reverse Hom transition Hom_R(M_j,N)→Hom_R(M_i,N) sends f to f∘u_ij, hence uses exactly the categorical precomposition operation already recorded from representable presheaves and functors of points. Module-linearity and preservation of identity/composition are respected, while direction-indexed system coherence and eventual-image stabilization defining the Mittag-Leffler condition remain parent-specific; the entire Hom inverse system is not identified with an arbitrary representable presheaf.

The affine-scheme and locally affine scheme formulations explicitly say 'isomorphic as a locally ringed space', meaning a morphism of locally ringed spaces with two-sided inverse in that category, respecting the continuous map, structure sheaves and local stalk maps. The existing generic categorical-isomorphism candidate requires f:X→Y and g:Y→X with gf=id_X and fg=id_Y, with no underlying-set bijection alone assumed. Instantiating its ambient category to locally ringed spaces gives exactly the same underlying invertibility prerequisite. This does NOT identify an arbitrary bijection or underlying topological homeomorphism with a locally ringed-space isomorphism; the category/morphism type stays explicit in the affine/scheme parent statements.

The interval-weight formulation defines orthogonality of distinct-degree p_n,p_m by ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)w(x)dx=0 for n≠m, with nonnegative integrable weight and finite absolute moments. The measure formulation defines the same mixed-inner-product vanishing ∫p_n(x)p_m(x)dμ(x)=0 for n≠m for a nonnegative measure μ. On the stated interval, define μ_w(B)=∫_{B∩(a,b)} w(x)dx; then dμ_w=w(x)dx and the two displayed orthogonality prerequisites coincide exactly. In the measure source μ may be more general (including singular Lebesgue–Stieltjes parts), so the measure-level prerequisite is the valid common abstraction; weights, density/absolute continuity, support, admissibility and moments remain distinctly specified in the full parent formulations. No claim that arbitrary μ must possess density w.

The original second discrete-time martingale variant states its process (X_n,F_n) is integrable, which means E|X_n|<∞ for each n≥0. The first discrete-time and continuous-time martingale formulations explicitly state E|X_t|<∞ at each index, without requiring a common bound, and the conditional-expectation source also uses integrability as finite absolute expectation. The sole shared prerequisite is coordinatewise L¹ integrability for a real random variable at each time parameter; specializing its index set T from nonnegative reals to nonnegative integers gives precisely the discrete-time condition. The process index set, adaptation, filtration, conditional expectation identities, and absence of a uniform L¹ bound remain specified in their respective full source formulations.

The full complete-local-ring formulation uses the canonical unital ring homomorphism R→lim_n R/m^n and requires this map to be an isomorphism. Its missing candidate explicitly requires a unital ring homomorphism having a unital ring-homomorphism inverse, not a mere bijection of underlying sets. This is exactly the generic categorical isomorphism prerequisite when the ambient category is unital commutative rings; in this category inverse arrows are ring homomorphisms.
